preamble: Eight solutions are individuals of a kind, not further defined in their clues

clue.text: Felicity warbles for Spooner's babies

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of neighbouring words, so the two words here trade their starts

parts.note: swap the opening sounds L and S of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone called Felicity croons to a pair of infants in the voice of the famous word-muddling clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sucklings are infants still being nursed at the breast, so the plural noun matches young babies.

clue.text: Outside American university keep quiet

indicators.note: one piece stands outside the other, wrapping round it

explanation.surface: A student is told to hush up while standing outside an American campus.
explanation.walkthrough: Delia Smith is a hugely popular British television cook, one of the eight cooks the preamble leaves undefined.
explanation.definitionFit: Delia Smith is a famous British cookery writer and television presenter, matching the preamble's group of celebrity cooks.

clue.text: Act to seal fracture

indicators.note: to seal something is to close it in, so one piece is shut inside the other

explanation.surface: An instruction to take action and plug a break, as a plumber or surgeon might.
explanation.walkthrough: Fanny Cradock was a flamboyant British television cook of the 1950s to 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Fanny Cradock was a celebrated mid-century British television chef, one of the preamble's eight cooks.

clue.text: Not totally agile, having injected drug

indicators.note: something injected goes inside, so one piece is put into the other
not the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: lithe means supple and agile; lose its last letter
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An athlete is a bit less nimble after an injection of some substance.
explanation.walkthrough: LITHE curtailed is LITH, and E is injected after its first letter. Prue Leith is a British restaurateur, cookery writer and television judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Prue Leith is a well-known British cook and cookery-show judge, one of the preamble's group of eight.

clue.text: Office employee that carries around important item of stationery

indicators.note: to carry something around is to hold it inside, so one word encloses the other

explanation.surface: A secretary carries a vital piece of office kit around the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office employee' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the piece that gets carried.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad is a pad of paper for jotting things down, a standard piece of desk stationery.

clue.text: Fight has beast rising over American slave

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the word is taken backwards

parts.note: a cat is a beast; it is read upwards

explanation.surface: A scene in an arena: a fight in which a wild animal rears up over an American.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' simply means the earlier pieces sit above the last one.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartacus was the Thracian gladiator and escaped slave who led a great revolt against Rome.

clue.text: Man whose welfare I don't care about, one up the pole?

definitions.text: Man whose welfare I don't care about
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the man in the selfish saying 'I'm all right, ...'
second meaning: a small flag flown from a staff, as in the Union one

explanation.surface: A heartless remark about a fellow, wondering if he is the one climbing the pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm all right, Jack' is a British phrase for selfish indifference to others; a jack is also a flag hoisted on a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is the one addressed in the selfish catchphrase, and the word also names a flag such as the Union flag on its staff.

clue.text: Bird circling very loudly about

indicators.note: something circling goes all the way round, so the bird word wraps the others

explanation.surface: A noisy bird wheels round and round, squawking at full volume.
explanation.walkthrough: Madhur Jaffrey is an actor and cookery writer who brought Indian cooking to British television.
explanation.definitionFit: Madhur Jaffrey is a renowned writer and broadcaster on Indian cuisine, one of the preamble's eight cooks.

clue.text: Sri Lanka, passionate and noisy

parts.note: the international vehicle registration code for Sri Lanka

explanation.surface: A description of Sri Lanka as an ardent, loud place.
explanation.walkthrough: CL is the car-sticker code for Sri Lanka, a less familiar one than GB or F.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamorous describes something making a loud outcry or din, a close synonym for noisy.

clue.text: Great obscurity about a person leading a double life?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the single letter

explanation.surface: A deep mystery surrounds someone who seems to have two separate lives, like a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double life' suggests a spy; the question mark flags the punning sense of two marriages.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigamist is married to two spouses at once, so literally keeps two households and lives twice over.

clue.text: Romantic involvement not excellent, always fighting

indicators.note: not means without, so those letters are removed from the first word

parts.note: A1 written as letters, meaning first-rate
ay is an old and poetic word for ever

explanation.surface: A love affair that's gone sour and is all quarrels.
explanation.walkthrough: AFFAIR minus AI leaves AFFR, then AY. AI stands for A1, top quality.
explanation.definitionFit: An affray is a public brawl or disturbance of the peace, so it is a scene of fighting.

clue.text: Doctor attached to huge hospital — not necessarily a big noise

parts.note: the Doctor in the long-running BBC series Doctor Who
OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A medic working at a giant hospital, who may not be an important figure there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big noise' suggests an important person; here it is a literal sound, and a soft rushing one.
explanation.definitionFit: A whoosh is the rushing sound of something moving fast through air, which can be quite soft rather than loud.

clue.text: Individual who has consumed for inner energy

indicators.note: one thing put for another means it takes that one's place, and inner points to a letter inside the word

explanation.surface: Someone who has eaten to restore their energy levels.
explanation.walkthrough: ATE replaces the inner E of PERSON. Jennifer Paterson was one of the 'Two Fat Ladies', a 1990s British cookery show.
explanation.definitionFit: Jennifer Paterson was a British television cook famous for the series Two Fat Ladies, fitting the preamble's group.

clue.text: Report of illegal bowler in a period of play

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: in cricket a bowler who throws rather than bowls is called a chucker, which is illegal

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire reports a bowler with a suspect action during play.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the arm must not straighten when bowling; a bowler who does so 'chucks' the ball illegally.
explanation.definitionFit: A chukka is one of the timed periods into which a polo match is divided.

clue.text: Chap lands abroad, offering something to seal the deal?

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A businessman arrives overseas and proposes a gesture to close the agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seal' suggests wax or a stamp; the question mark marks the definition as a description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaking hands traditionally confirms an agreement, so a firm grip of hands is what finalises a bargain.

clue.text: A label to get cut immediately

parts.note: to lance is to cut open with a blade

explanation.surface: Someone needs a price label snipped off without delay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means seen or understood instantly, with only a quick look needed, hence straight away.

clue.text: Formal attire that might bother the violinist

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bow tie worn with evening dress
second meaning: dicky means unreliable or faulty, and a violinist plays with a bow

explanation.surface: A musician in evening dress is troubled by something about the outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky is British slang for shaky or unsound, as in a dicky heart; a faulty bow would trouble a string player.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the British informal name for a bow tie, and read literally it is a defective bow for a fiddle.

clue.text: Support for writers not often seen these days?

definitions.text: Support for writers not often seen these days?

parts.note: surface reading: encouragement or funding for authors, which is becoming scarce

parts.words: Support for writers not often seen these days?
parts.note: setter's reading: writers are pens, and the support is a desk stand holding pens and ink bottles, now rarely seen

explanation.surface: A lament that authors get little backing nowadays.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkstand is a stand on a desk holding ink pots and pens, an old-fashioned item rarely used now.

clue.text: Discharge rising female model wanting external influence

indicators.note: wanting something outside means it needs a wrapper placed around it

parts.note: to have a say is to have influence

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from the bottom up, so the pair is turned round

parts.note: an artist's model sits for a portrait

explanation.surface: A woman model gets up and leaves, lacking any outside pull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' looks like letting something out; here it means paying off a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge an obligation or debt is to fulfil it, which is one sense of satisfy, as in satisfying a creditor.

clue.text: Movement of the absurd mother crossing platform

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across something, so the outer word spans and encloses the other

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A ridiculous scene of a mother clambering across a stage.
explanation.walkthrough: DAM goes across DAIS: DA-DAIS-M.
explanation.definitionFit: Dadaism was the early twentieth-century art movement that embraced nonsense and irrationality.

clue.text: Headline in slant across page

indicators.note: one thing lying across another covers it, so the slant word goes round the single letter

parts.note: the slash is the slanting punctuation mark /

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline set in italics across a page.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is a newspaper's big front-page story or banner headline in journalists' jargon.

clue.text: Laurie? Child looked after and sheltered

parts.note: Laurie Lee, the English author of Cider with Rosie
a ward is a child in someone's care

explanation.surface: Laurie, a child brought up in care, was protected.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurie Lee was an English writer best known for his memoir of a Cotswold childhood, Cider with Rosie.
explanation.definitionFit: The leeward side is the side away from the wind, hence the side that is protected from it.

clue.text: Hurried, being guided after injury in street

indicators.note: after puts the guided piece second, behind the street-and-injury chunk
in places one piece inside the other

explanation.surface: Someone hurt in the road was helped along quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To scuttle is to run with short quick steps, so the past tense scuttled matches hurried.

clue.text: Fulfil the function of college

parts.note: to be a thing is to serve as it
Eton College, the English public school

explanation.surface: A phrase about what a college is for.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Beeton wrote the Victorian Book of Household Management, the classic British cookery book.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella Beeton was the Victorian author of a famous household management and recipe book, one of the preamble's cooks.

clue.text: Ex-PM has changed sides, is sent flying

indicators.note: switching sides means swapping right for left, so one letter is exchanged for its opposite

parts.note: Gordon Brown, UK Prime Minister 2007 to 2010

explanation.surface: A former prime minister defects to another party and is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) in BROWN becomes L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Blown describes something carried off through the air by wind, in other words propelled into flight.

clue.text: Begins as map-maker holding drawing implement

indicators.note: holding means having something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the Ordnance Survey, Britain's national mapping agency

explanation.surface: A cartographer starts work, pen in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ordnance Survey is the official British map-making body, so OS is a map-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: To open is to start, as a play or meeting opens, so opens works as a verb for starts.

clue.text: Disciple following body of divine commandments

indicators.note: following sends the disciple piece second, behind the commandments piece

parts.note: the religious law, as in the Law of Moses
a disciple can be called a son of his master

explanation.surface: A follower obeying the Ten Commandments.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigella Lawson is a British food writer and television cook.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigella Lawson is a popular British cookery writer and broadcaster, one of the eight cooks in the preamble.

clue.text: One admiring the statement from char not on early duty

parts.note: a char, or cleaning lady, does the cleaning, so she says she does
on a later shift rather than an early one

explanation.surface: A cleaner explains she is on the late shift, and someone admires her for it.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a British term for a cleaning woman; char also suggests tea or burnt food.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships idols, and more loosely is someone who adores or admires a person excessively.

clue.text: Pretty bunch with ace standing out

indicators.note: something standing out is not included, so that letter is left out

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: An attractive group, one of whom is a star performer who stands out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' looks like the definition (sprightly); it is part of the wordplay. Constance Spry was a British florist and cookery writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Constance Spry co-wrote the Constance Spry Cookery Book, so she belongs among the preamble's eight cooks.

clue.text: Furious females making chaps at Brussels face day of reckoning

parts.note: Brussels is home to the European Union institutions
the Ides of March, Caesar's fatal day

explanation.surface: Angry women see men in Brussels brought to account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Furious' looks like plain anger; it points to the Furies of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eumenides is a name for the Furies, the avenging goddesses of Greek mythology, who were female.
